description: AI adoption stalls not because of weak tools or insufficient training, but because learning remains invisible. Generative AI requires employees to redesign their own workflows, and in uncertain environments many experiment quietly—or not at all. What drives meaningful adoption is peer influence. When employees see trusted colleagues using AI in real tasks, sharing tips, modeling guardrails, and discussing both successes and missteps, AI feels safe, practical, and relevant. For managers, the takeaway is clear: focus less on mandates and more on visibility. Encourage consistent messaging, create forums for shared learning, model your own AI use, and reward employees who share practical examples. Build psychological safety and strong cross-team connections. When experimentation is visible and socially supported, adoption accelerates naturally.
title: Peer Influence Can Make or Break Your AI Rollout
